chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn Hassan, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
How ugly it would be for the believer if there were a desire for him which disgraces him.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean for a desire to disgrace a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies a specific desire (*raghba*) that enslaves the soul as a source of spiritual humiliation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere poverty, but as freedom from the tyranny of base appetites. This teaching underscores the practical implication that unchecked worldly attachment compromises a believer's dignity and autonomy, a theme central to the ethical teachings of the Ahl al-Bayt. It serves as a reminder that true nobility lies in mastering one's desires rather than being mastered by them.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ali Bin Hassan, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘How ugly it would be with the Momin if there happens to be a desire for him which disgraces him’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ali ibn Hassan from those who narrated to him from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
How disgraceful to a believer is a desire that humiliates him!”’
